first_impression.reaction: Sophie here. We haven't even picked a wedding destination yet, so the honeymoon is the bit we keep putting off. The opening line tells me what this is in one go, and the second paragraph basically describes my evenings: 'every spare evening goes to guest lists and suppliers.' So I kept going. I skimmed the how-it-works part, read the wedding-and-honeymoon section and the questions list properly. James would read the takeaways and the passport bit and stop.

journey.quote: The good ones agree their fee and confirm what is included in writing before you commit to anything.
journey.reaction: Fee and inclusions in writing up front is exactly what I want to hear when the fear is hidden costs. Good start.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: The work is in keeping those pieces in step, so a change of date in one place is carried through everywhere else.
journey.reaction: That's the actual value, said plainly. One change, one conversation, not me emailing four hotels.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: the kind of places that make you both exhale
journey.reaction: Slightly precious, but it isn't a fairytale cliché, so I'll let it go.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Wedded Wonderland offers destination honeymoon planning and travel concierge as a service, and planning a honeymoon on its own follows the same Wedded Advisor process as Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: This reads like a corporate services page. I had to read it twice to work out that it means 'we do honeymoons on their own too, same process'.

journey.section: Meet your Wedded Advisor and agree the fee
journey.quote: So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.
journey.reaction: I got it the first time. By this point 'fee in writing' has come up in the intro, the takeaways and the sentence right before this one, and it comes up again in the questions, the FAQ and the close. It starts to feel like the page is leaning on the one thing it can say about cost.

journey.section: Meet your Wedded Advisor and agree the fee
journey.quote: Your advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: Yes. Mum and Dad are putting money in and they'll want one number in dollars, not euros and baht.

journey.section: Planning the honeymoon alongside your wedding
journey.quote: The wedding week ends, the guests fly home and the two of you move on to the next stay without starting a new conversation with someone new.
journey.reaction: This is the section that's actually about us. Nice idea, but it stays general. I'd want to see what that handover morning looks like in practice: who sorts the transfer while we're hungover and the last guests are leaving.

journey.quote: Born in Australia and married overseas? You will always need a name change certificate for your passport.
journey.reaction: I genuinely didn't know this, and it's the kind of thing that bites you at the airport. This is the insider detail I trust. I'd send this bit to James.

journey.section: What to decide before you enquire
journey.quote: Each of you names one or two things the trip must include.
journey.reaction: Practical and a bit fun. We could actually do this over dinner. The payment-order point is useful too, given the parents are paying for part of it.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: These are worth asking whoever you speak to, including us.
journey.reaction: Fair, and not pushy. The insolvency and exchange-rate questions are the ones I'd never have thought of. Dad will like those.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: Do you receive commission from suppliers? A straightforward question deserves a straightforward answer, and it tells you how the planner is paid on top of any fee.
journey.reaction: Good question. The obvious next thought is: so what's yours? The page tells me to ask but doesn't answer it for Wedded Wonderland.

journey.quote: A fee only means something next to what it covers. Ask for the fee in writing, before any work begins, along with the inclusions, and compare planners on both.
journey.reaction: This is the question I'd actually type into Google, and the answer dodges it. Not even a range or what it depends on. As a lawyer, I notice a non-answer.

journey.quote: A honeymoon should feel like the easy part.
journey.reaction: Calm, no hard sell. I like that the close doesn't shout at me.

unanswered_questions: How is the fee charged (flat, percentage, commission) and roughly what does it come to for a two-week honeymoon? The page says it's agreed in writing but not what it's based on.
Does Wedded Wonderland take supplier commissions on top of the fee, given the article tells me to ask?
Do you hold insolvency insurance, given the article tells me to ask?
If we book the wedding and the honeymoon with you, is it literally the same Wedded Advisor for both?
Is there a real couple (destination and date) whose wedding week and honeymoon you planned back to back?
Are there any extras or perks from booking the honeymoon through you rather than direct?

turn_offs_found.quote: A fee only means something next to what it covers.
turn_offs_found.why: No figures or ranges are given, so the couple cannot judge the fee before enquiring (deferred business detail).

would_share_with: James (partner): the key takeaways and the name-on-your-tickets section
Mum and Dad, since they're contributing: the questions list, especially insolvency insurance and exchange rates

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, speak with Wedded Concierge and tell us anything.
cta_reaction.why: Low pressure, which I like. But we haven't picked a wedding destination, I still don't know how the fee works and I haven't seen a real wedding or honeymoon you've done. I'd bookmark this, click the 'when to go on honeymoon' guide and the honeymoon packages first, and come back once we have a destination.

top_3_changes: Make the 'alongside your wedding' section concrete with one handover scenario (the morning after: guests leaving, luggage, the transfer to the next stay, a late check-out) so it reads like someone who has done it, not a general idea. That's the bit that's actually about couples like us.
Cut the repeated 'fee in writing' line, starting with 'So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.' Once in the intro, once in the steps and once in the close is plenty.

Rewrite the opener of 'How it works' ('offers destination honeymoon planning and travel concierge as a service') in plain words, and make the FAQ cost answer feel less like a dodge, for example by saying plainly that the page can't give a figure and what to compare instead.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (Sydney, early research, 14 months out, parents contributing, no spreadsheets)
No invented brand facts; anything the page doesn't say is listed in unanswered_questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments ignored as invisible
Didn't invent problems; positives recorded where the draft earns them
Business-deferred details (fee basis, commissions, insolvency cover, same advisor, real honeymoons, perks, Wedded Privileges) kept to unanswered_questions, not top_3_changes

assumptions: Persona is provisional (not CRM-calibrated), so these reactions reflect the assumed profile.
Arrival context not specified; read as if arriving from a Google search for 'honeymoon planning service'.
Fee basis, commissions, on-the-ground presence, real-honeymoon proof and perks are deferred by the business, so they appear only as unanswered questions.
